observed: Used the Browser pane tab-1 (a new tab was refused because the pane was at its tab cap, so I reused a leftover tab after clearing its localStorage, sessionStorage and the two _ga cookies for localhost). For each of four combinations I set the viewport and colour scheme, loaded http://localhost:4180/ fresh, ran an in-page script, then took a screenshot. 1) 1440x900 light: documentElement.scrollWidth 1440 = innerWidth 1440; no visible text element under 13px (smallest 13.5px); body text #1b1b18 on #fbfaf7 = 16.54:1; main links #b4441c on #fbfaf7 = 5.32:1 (hosts.md link on its panel #f2f0ea = 4.87:1); nav links 16.54:1; selected tab 'Any agent' text #1b1b18 = 16.54:1 against the page background (15.15:1 against its own panel #f2f0ea). 2) 1440x900 dark: 1440 = 1440; nothing under 13px (smallest 13.5px); body #ecebe6 on #141413 = 15.44:1; main links #f08a5d = 7.46:1 (hosts.md on panel #1d1d1b = 6.83:1); selected tab 15.44:1 vs page (14.14:1 vs panel). 3) mobile 375x812 light (Pixel UA, 2x): scrollWidth 375 = innerWidth 375; nothing under 13px; same colour pairs and ratios as desktop light (16.54, 5.32, 4.87, 16.54). 4) mobile 375x812 dark: 375 = 375; nothing under 13px; ratios as desktop dark (15.44, 7.46, 6.83, 15.44). A wider scan of every visible text element found zero below AA (4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text) at all four combinations; the lowest ratio on the page is 4.87:1. Document text is identical at all four (22859 characters, same hash, same h1, same six h2s, 35 links), so the screenshots show the same content; text in all four screenshots is legible. At 375 wide 40 visible elements extend past the viewport edge, but every one sits inside an intentional overflow-x:auto scroller (header nav, install tablist, npx code block, proof-table wrapper); html and body overflow-x are visible, so the equal scrollWidth is real. Viewport reset to desktop at the end.
expected: scrollWidth equals innerWidth at every combination (1440 and 375, light and dark); no visible text with computed font-size below 13px; body text, links and selected tab text each at least 4.5:1 against the page background in both schemes; four screenshots show the same content with legible text.
notes: 1) The evidence folder already held files from earlier S3 runs (no r7- prefix); I left them untouched and saved only r7-* files. 2) The app is a Vite dev server being edited live; both styles.css (t=1791703058846) and App.jsx (t=1791703061706) were identical across all four loads and no HMR update arrived during the run, but a later build could differ. 3) Screenshots are viewport captures only: desktop 800x500 (downscaled from 1440x900), mobile 750x1624; mobile shows just the top of the page. Lower content was covered by the whole-document in-page scans, not by screenshots. 4) At 375 wide the header nav shows 'Models' cut off and 'GitHub' hidden until the nav is scrolled sideways, and the install tablist hides 'Codex plugin' and 'Git clone' the same way; these are inner scrollers, not page scroll, so they do not violate the criterion, but they are discoverability friction. 5) The contrast pairs were computed against the page background as asked; the selected tab sits on a panel colour (#f2f0ea light, #1d1d1b dark) and passes against that too (15.15 and 14.14). The selected tab text colour is the same as body text; it is marked by an accent underline, not colour. 6) The page requests a Google Fonts stylesheet (fonts.googleapis.com, opaque status 0 in resource timing, fonts rendered). 7) Before my run the leftover tab held localStorage oldhand-analytics-consent=denied plus _ga cookies for localhost, so analytics cookies had been set in that tab at some point despite a stored 'denied'; I did not investigate (outside this scenario). 8) Old console errors from earlier sessions (a Vite SyntaxError on App.jsx, a websocket failure, a 404) sit in the same tab buffer before my first load; none occurred during this run.
